joints.name: clay_gp_mortar_bed_ec6
joints.note: Clay unit Group 1, general-purpose mortar M10, f_b = 20 MPa, f_m = 10 MPa. Cohesion f_vk0 = 0.30 MPa (Table 3.4, M10-M20). Tension: the code gives the flexural strength f_xk1 = 0.10 MPa (§3.6.3, failure plane parallel to the bed), a bending strength through Z = b t^2 / 6; the engine's tension is direct and its rigid-plastic hinge gives M = f_t A t / 2 = 3 f_t Z, so the direct value that reproduces the code moment is f_xk1 / 3 = 0.0333 MPa (DESIGN §10, slice 5 close). Friction 0.4 from the 0.4 sigma_d term of eq. 3.5. Cap 0.065 f_b = 0.065 x 20 = 1.30 MPa. Compression eq. 3.2 f_k = K f_b^0.7 f_m^0.3 with K = 0.55 (Table 3.3): 0.55 x 20^0.7 x 10^0.3 = 0.55 x 8.1418 x 1.9953 = 8.935, taken as 8.93 MPa. Stiffness: E = K_E f_k with K_E = 1000 (§3.7.2) is the modulus of the masonry, unit and joint together; in a rigid-block model one joint spring carries a whole course's deformation, so the spring is E / (h_unit + h_joint) = 8.93 GPa / (0.065 + 0.010) m = 119 GPa/m normal; G = 0.4 E (§3.7.3): 47.6 GPa/m tangential.

joints.name: clay_gp_mortar_perpend_ec6
joints.note: A filled perpend in the same general-purpose mortar: the same unit-mortar bond as the bed row, so cohesion, tension, friction, cap and stiffness are the bed row's. EN 1996-1-1 gives no strength for the perpend joint itself: eq. 3.6 (0.5 f_vk0, cap 0.045 f_b) is the shear strength along the BED of a wall whose perpends are unfilled, and f_xk2 is a wall flexural strength whose failure plane runs through the units, so neither describes this joint (DESIGN §10, slice 5 close). An unfilled perpend is a dry joint: use a dry profile, not this row.

joints.name: clay_gp_mortar_bed_gooch_mean
joints.note: Gooch et al. 2023/2025, 1:1:6 mortar on Australian clay brick. Direct tension 0.20 MPa, the middle of the measured 0.15-0.25 (a direct value: no flexural conversion). Cohesion 0.60 MPa, just above the low end of the couplet shear bond 0.58-1.04. Friction 1.05, within the 1.04-1.16 measured at 0.22 MPa normal stress (the fitted mu = 1.12 e^(-0.35 sigma_n) gives 1.04 there). No shear cap measured. Compression and stiffness are not measured there: the code row's values.

joints.name: lime_mortar_handmade_brick_upc_mean
joints.note: Segura, Pela, Saloustros and Roca, triplet tests: c = 0.16 MPa, phi = 33.71 deg, mu = tan 33.71 deg = 0.667169. No tension measured; the dry-bond floor. No shear cap measured. Compression and stiffness are not measured there: the EC6 code row's values, which overstate a lime mortar's compression.

joints.name: c24_bearing_perp_to_grain
joints.source: https://www.svenskttra.se/siteassets/5-publikationer/pdfer/sw-design-of-timber-structures-vol3-2022.pdf ; https://finesoftware.eu/help/truss4/en/compression-perpendicular-to-the-grain-in-supports-01/ ; https://blueprints.readthedocs.io/en/stable/API%20reference/codes/eurocode/en_338_2016/chapter_5_classification_of_structural_timber/table_1/ (EN 338 Table 1) ; Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-190 ch. 4 (Glass and Zelinka 2010)
joints.note: C24 perpendicular to grain: f_c,90,k = 2.5 MPa x k_c,90 = 1.5 (solid timber on discrete supports) = 3.75 MPa (Swedish Wood Vol. 3 Ex 3.2; EN 1995-1-1 §6.1.5). No tension, no cohesion. Friction 0.3, the low end of the Wood Handbook range 0.3 to 0.5 for smooth dry wood on hard smooth surfaces (kinetic), matched through a search snippet, PDF unopened. Stiffness over the 45 mm joist width b of Ex 3.2, the one bearing dimension the example gives: E_90,mean = 0.37 GPa (EN 338 C24) / 0.045 m = 8.2 GPa/m normal, G_mean = 0.69 GPa (EN 338 C24) / 0.045 m = 15.3 GPa/m tangential. A different bearing depth re-derives both.

fasteners.name: ec5_screw_8x60_steel_to_glulam
fasteners.note: Swedish Wood Vol. 3 Ex 4.1: 8 x 60 mm screw, f_u = 410 MPa, 8 mm steel plate, GL30c (rho_k 390, rho_m 430 kg/m3); modes c/d/e 9.91 / 4.83 / 5.26 kN, so 4.83 kN per shear plane (mode d). Withdrawal by EN 1995-1-1/A1:2008 §8.7.2 with the example's own inputs: penetration 60 - 8 = 52 mm, l_ef = 52 - d = 44 mm, alpha = 90 deg, k_d = min(d/8, 1) = 1; f_ax,k = 0.52 d^-0.5 l_ef^-0.1 rho_k^0.8 = 14.89 MPa; F_ax,Rk = f_ax,k d l_ef = 14.89 x 8 x 44 = 5242 N, taken as 5.24 kN (the Structural Basics 1.74 kN is a 2.5 mm screw and is not this row). Caveat: l_ef = 44 mm is below the 6 d = 48 mm minimum point-side threaded penetration that §8.7.2 is recalled to require, so the formula is applied just outside its range; verify against the text. Slip modulus EN 1995-1-1 Table 7.1, screws: K_ser = rho_m^1.5 d / 23 = 430^1.5 x 8 / 23 = 3101 N/mm, x 2 for steel-to-timber (§7.1(3)) = 6203 N/mm = 6.20 MN/m per shear plane per screw. Bearing: the C24 3.75 MPa and 8.2 GPa/m of the member it bears on (the example's glulam is stiffer; the C24 row is the one the catalogue carries).

fasteners.name: ec5_ring_nail_4x40_steel_plate
fasteners.note: Swedish Wood Vol. 3 Ex 4.2: 4.0 x 40 mm ring-shank nail through a 5 mm plate into GL30c (rho_k 390, rho_m 430 kg/m3), 1.607 kN as published; a recomputation gives about 1.48 kN. Withdrawal 0.42 kN is the Structural Basics datum for a 3.1 mm ring-shank nail at 55 mm penetration (f_ax,k = 2.45 MPa), not this nail. Slip modulus EN 1995-1-1 Table 7.1, nails without predrilling: K_ser = rho_m^1.5 d^0.8 / 30 = 430^1.5 x 4^0.8 / 30 = 901 N/mm, x 2 for steel-to-timber (§7.1(3)) = 1802 N/mm = 1.80 MN/m per nail. Bearing: the C24 3.75 MPa and 8.2 GPa/m of the member it bears on.

fasteners.name: ec5_bolt_m16_double_shear
fasteners.note: Swedish Wood Vol. 3 Ex 4.3: M16 bolt, f_u = 360 MPa, 8 mm outer steel plates (t = 0.5 d) on a 90 mm GL30c member (rho_k 390, rho_m 430 kg/m3), modes j/k: 12.9 kN (mode k). EN 1995-1-1 §8.2.3(1) defines those expressions per shear plane per fastener (the 0.5 in mode j is the central member split between its two planes), so 12.9 kN is per shear plane and the bolt carries 25.8 kN across its two planes. No withdrawal given. Slip modulus EN 1995-1-1 Table 7.1, bolts: K_ser = rho_m^1.5 d / 23 = 430^1.5 x 16 / 23 = 6203 N/mm, x 2 for steel-to-timber (§7.1(3)) = 12406 N/mm = 12.4 MN/m per shear plane per bolt. Bearing: the C24 3.75 MPa and 8.2 GPa/m of the member it bears on.

materials.name: clay_brick
materials.source: EN 1991-1-1 Annex A, Table A.1 (masonry units) ; the brick fixtures of ANCHORS.md (B-CAT-01, 10 x 8 dry wall)
materials.note: Solid fired-clay brick at 2000 kg/m3, the density every brick fixture in this repository uses (B-CAT-01: a 0.215 x 0.1025 x 0.065 m brick of 2.8648 kg). A perforated unit is lighter and needs its own row. Compressive strength 20 MPa is a typical declared normalised unit strength f_b (EN 771-1, tested to EN 772-1), not a measured value; it only ranks which body of a crushing joint crushes.

materials.name: c24
materials.note: C24 softwood mean density rho_mean = 420 kg/m3 (characteristic rho_k = 350). Mass is a mean quantity, so the mean is used. Compressive strength 2.5 MPa is f_c,90,k (EN 338:2016 Table 1), the across-grain value timber bears at in these structures; it only ranks which body of a crushing joint crushes.
